renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: caller_yield_dots
  title: Peak yield and agreement by caller
  description: |-
    Each dot is a sample and peak caller: its colour is the number of peaks the caller made (log10) and its size is the share of those peaks the other caller reproduced. It answers how much each caller called and how much the two agree.
    How to read: large dots mean the other caller confirmed most of the peaks. A small dot with a dark colour is a caller that made many peaks the other did not. Read it with the unique peaks bars before trusting either caller.
    Note: neither caller is a subset of the other, so disagreement is informative and not an error.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: caller
    mean_expression: log10_n_peaks
    frac_expressing: frac_shared

- component: figure
  id: caller_peak_scatter
  title: Peaks against the other caller
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample and peak caller: the peaks that caller made on the vertical axis against the peaks the other caller made on the horizontal axis, coloured by target. It answers which caller is more productive for each target.
    How to read: a point far from the equal-count diagonal means one caller called many more peaks than the other, so look at its unique peaks and at the target. Each sample appears twice, once per caller, with the axes swapped.
    Note: the equal-count diagonal is not drawn, and a caller with no peaks has no point on a log axis.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: n_peaks_other
    y: n_peaks
    color: target
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    hover_name: sample
    labels:
      n_peaks_other: Peaks from the other caller
      n_peaks: Peaks from this caller
      target: Target

- component: figure
  id: caller_unique_bar
  title: Peaks the other caller did not reproduce
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and peak caller: the number of its peaks that the other caller did not reproduce. It answers how much each caller sees alone.
    How to read: a tall bar means that caller made many peaks the other missed. Compare the two bars of a sample, and check its target, since the callers suit different kinds of mark.
    Note: a peak counts as reproduced when it overlaps at least one peak of the other caller on the same chromosome.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median number of peaks the other caller did not make of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/cutandrun.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: n_unique
    color: caller
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      n_unique: Peaks the other caller did not make
      caller: Caller
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: n_unique

- component: figure
  id: caller_shared_bar
  title: Share of peaks the other caller reproduced
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and peak caller: the fraction of its peaks that the other caller also made. It answers how reproducible each caller's peaks are across the two methods.
    How to read: a value near 1 means the other caller confirmed nearly all of the peaks. A caller that made few peaks can score high while the other scores low, so read this beside the peak counts.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of peaks reproduced by the other caller of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/cutandrun.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: frac_shared
    color: caller
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      frac_shared: Share of peaks reproduced
      caller: Caller
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: frac_shared

- component: card
  title: Peaks called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peaks called, and the bars split it by peak caller. It answers how productive each caller was.
    How to read: SEACR and MACS2 differ by design, so unequal totals are common. A caller with almost nothing for a sample is worth checking against the signal tracks.
  column: n_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: Peaks, by caller

- component: card
  title: Average peak reproduction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of peaks that the other caller reproduced, and the box shows the spread over samples and callers. It answers how well the two callers agree overall.
    How to read: a narrow box near 1 means strong agreement. A wide box mixes samples where the callers agree with samples where they diverge.
  column: frac_shared
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: pl.col('n_peaks') > 0
  caption: Share reproduced, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Least reproduced peak set
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest share of peaks reproduced by the other caller, shown with the median and the highest. It answers which peak set agrees least.
    How to read: a minimum far below the median is a caller and sample to inspect. Check its peak count first, since few peaks make the share unstable.
    Note: the nf-core pipeline gives no pass mark for this share, so none is drawn.
  column: frac_shared
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  filter_expr: pl.col('n_peaks') > 0
  caption: Least reproduced, with the median and the best

- component: card
  title: Median peak width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the per-sample median peak widths in base pairs, and the histogram shows how they spread. It answers how broad the peaks are.
    How to read: widths differ between callers and between targets, so a spread is expected. The pipeline advises broad peak mode for epitopes with a wide range such as histone marks, and narrow mode for small binding proteins.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: median_width
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  filter_expr: pl.col('n_peaks') > 0
  caption: Median peak width, by sample and caller

- component: card
  title: Peaks seen by one caller only
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peaks that the other caller did not reproduce, and the bar splits it by caller. It answers which caller sees more on its own.
    How to read: a lopsided bar shows one caller finds many peaks the other does not. Open the unique peaks bars to see which samples drive it.
  column: n_unique
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: caller
  caption: Peaks seen alone, by caller

- component: table
  title: Peak caller agreement table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and peak caller, with the peak count, total and median width, and how many peaks the other caller reproduced or did not. It answers the exact counts behind the figures.
    How to read: sort by the shared fraction to find the weakest agreement, and check the peak count beside it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: figure
  id: frip_composition_bar
  title: Fragment coverage inside and outside peaks
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample split into the share of its fragment coverage that falls inside its own called peaks and the share that falls outside them. It answers how much of the signal the peaks capture.
    How to read: a larger in-peaks share means a better signal-to-noise ratio. The nf-core cutandrun documentation reads a FRiP above 0.3 as reasonable and above 0.7 as the highest quality. Low values point to background, few peaks or a peak threshold set very high.
    Note: SEACR reports no read counts, so coverage is the summed region signal scaled by the spike-in factor. The score also depends on the peak caller settings.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: fraction
    color: signal_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      fraction: Share of fragment coverage
      signal_class: Signal

- component: card
  title: Fragment coverage in and out of peaks
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total fragment coverage in base pairs, and the ring splits it into inside and outside the called peaks. It answers how much of the run falls in peaks.
    How to read: a large in-peaks share is good. A ring dominated by outside peaks means a noisy run or too few peaks called.
  column: coverage_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: signal_class
  caption: Coverage, inside and outside peaks

- component: card
  title: Average FRiP
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fraction of fragments in peaks, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how good the signal-to-noise ratio is overall.
    How to read: the nf-core cutandrun documentation reads a FRiP above 0.3 as reasonable and above 0.7 as the highest quality. A long lower whisker is a sample to open in the bar chart.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: frip
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: FRiP, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Lowest FRiP
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest fraction of fragments in peaks of any sample, shown with the median and the highest, against a floor of 0.3. It answers whether every sample reaches a reasonable signal-to-noise ratio.
    How to read: a sample below the floor has a lot of background or few peaks, so check its peak caller settings and its IgG control before using it.
    Lines and annotations: the floor of 0.3 is the level the nf-core cutandrun documentation calls reasonable, after Landt et al.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: frip
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.3
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: Lowest sample, against the 0.3 floor

- component: table
  title: FRiP table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a signal class, with the coverage in base pairs, the fraction, the sample FRiP, the peak count and the spike-in scale factor. It answers the exact numbers behind the figure.
    How to read: the sample FRiP is repeated on both rows of a sample. Sort by it to find the weakest sample.

- component: figure
  id: sample_design_bar
  title: Libraries per target
  description: |-
    Each bar is a target of the experiment: the number of libraries sequenced for it, coloured by whether it is a profiled target or an IgG control. It answers how the design is balanced.
    How to read: targets should have comparable library counts, and an IgG control should be present for the peak caller. A target without a control or with a single library cannot be called against a background or checked for reproducibility.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: target
    y: n_libraries
    color: role
    labels:
      target: Target
      n_libraries: Libraries
      role: Role

- component: card
  title: Samples, by role
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples, shown with the libraries behind them and the largest library count of a sample, and the ring splits the samples into profiled targets and IgG controls. It answers how many samples the run holds.
    How to read: a ring without an IgG control share means the peak caller had no background to call against.
  column: n_libraries
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - sum
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: role
  caption: Samples, by role

- component: card
  title: Targets
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct targets, shown with the count of samples, and the bars rank the targets by their samples. It answers which targets are best replicated.
    How to read: a target with a single sample has no replicate to compare.
  column: target
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: target
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: Samples per target

- component: card
  title: Libraries per target
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of libraries, and the bar splits it by target. It answers where the sequencing effort went.
    How to read: an even split means a balanced design. A target with far fewer libraries has less power.
  column: n_libraries
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: target
  caption: Libraries, by target

- component: card
  title: Replicate depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest replicate number in the run, shown with the median and the lowest. It answers how many replicates the design has.
    How to read: two or more replicates per target allow reproducibility to be checked. A maximum of 1 means no replicates.
  column: replicate
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: Highest replicate, with the median and lowest

- component: interactive
  id: sample_replicate_filter
  title: Replicate
  description: Pick one or more replicates to keep only their samples in the tiles that follow.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: replicate_label

- component: interactive
  id: sample_target_filter
  title: Target
  description: Pick one or more targets, including the IgG control, to keep only their samples in the tiles
    that follow.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: target

- component: table
  title: Sample table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its target, replicate, role, the control it was called against and the libraries behind it. It answers how the samples map to the files of the run.
    How to read: check that every target row names a control and that replicates are numbered as expected.
